incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure (water, energy, chemical, manufacturing, food)
incidents.vector: Actors use AI-generated exploitation scripts disguised as monitoring tools, plus internet-scanning services and the snap7 library, to find and access internet-exposed Siemens S7 PLCs running outdated or default-credentialed software.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warned of an active campaign conducting read/write reconnaissance on Siemens S7 PLCs to pre-position for future disruption of industrial processes; the alert coincides with US warnings about Iranian targeting of water systems but stops short of attribution.

incidents.victim: Multiple large manufacturers (GE, Philips, Shell, Toast, Zebra among claimed victims)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution zero-day (CVE-2026-12569) in PTC Windchill and FlexPLM product-lifecycle software, using a purpose-built web shell for credential theft and bulk data exfiltration.
incidents.impact: The Clop extortion group began threatening victims in mid-July after stealing data from dozens of organizations; fallout is still expanding as companies hunt for compromise, mirroring Clop's earlier MOVEit and Oracle EBS mass-exploitation campaigns.

incidents.victim: Latvia Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in an internet-exposed CSDD system after targeted preparation, accessing historical payment-receipt data going back to 2008.
incidents.impact: Data on roughly 1.2 million people and 200,000 businesses (about two-thirds of Latvia's population) was exposed; the president called it a national-security threat and the agency's supervisory board resigned.

incidents.victim: CareCloud (electronic health record provider)
incidents.vector: A hacker accessed one of CareCloud's AWS environments for roughly eight hours over March 10-16 and exfiltrated data.
incidents.impact: CareCloud told federal regulators that 3.7 million people had data exposed, including Social Security numbers, ID numbers, payment card data, and medical and insurance information; no group claimed the attack.

incidents.victim: Slovakia national traffic-camera network
incidents.vector: Slovakia's NBU found NERO R-ONE speed cameras — rebranded Russian CORDON PRO.M units bought via a Cyprus shell company — contained a backdoor that executes code sent via SMS from hardcoded Russian phone numbers, with SecureBoot disabled and passwordless live streams.
incidents.impact: 279 cameras from a €30 million EU-funded project were installed on Slovak roads before the backdoor and multiple additional vulnerabilities were discovered; deployment was paused pending an independent audit.

incidents.victim: Taiwan government agencies (Ministry of Digital Affairs)
incidents.vector: A Chinese-language operator ran a multi-agent AI framework (built on OpenClaw and Hermes) using up to eight coordinated subagents to autonomously conduct reconnaissance, crack credentials, exploit vulnerabilities, exfiltrate personnel records, and install backdoors across 12 attack waves.
incidents.impact: Described by researchers as the first 'near-autonomous' AI attack on a nation-state; Taiwan's MODA confirmed abnormal AI-driven attacks on government agencies detected in July, with secondary/backup systems used as springboards.

incidents.victim: Winnipeg Health Sciences Centre
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack disabled building systems tied to physical access control and climate control.
incidents.impact: Access doors and HVAC at Winnipeg's largest hospital were disabled and the access-card system taken offline, forcing increased on-site security; the hospital said patient care and clinical operations were not impacted.

incidents.victim: 144 US universities, foreign universities, companies and government agencies
incidents.vector: The Iran-based Mabna Institute ran spearphishing campaigns against professor accounts, compromising credentials to steal research and intellectual property on behalf of the IRGC and other Iranian clients.
incidents.impact: A superseding indictment charged 17 Iranians in a campaign running since 2013 that compromised ~8,000 professor accounts across 144 US and 178 foreign universities and stole 31.5 terabytes of data; a $10 million reward was offered for five defendants.

incidents.victim: 500+ organizations, heavily healthcare sector
incidents.vector: Medusa ransomware-as-a-service affiliates buy access from initial-access brokers and exploit unpatched web-facing software (e.g., Fortra GoAnywhere, BeyondTrust), sometimes weaponizing exploits within 24 hours or before public disclosure.
incidents.impact: An updated FBI/CISA/HHS advisory reported Medusa victims jumped from 300 to more than 500 in about a year, with the healthcare sector a frequent target; the group uses living-off-the-land techniques and legitimate remote-monitoring tools.

incidents.victim: Multiple Fortune 500 enterprises (McDonald's, Vodafone, Kyndryl, Gap and hotel chains among claims)
incidents.vector: An actor using the handle 'TheHatman' claims to have used compromised credentials, MFA fatigue and password spraying to exfiltrate employee data from victims' Microsoft Entra (Azure) tenants.
incidents.impact: From Aug 1-17 the actor advertised employee data of nearly a dozen large enterprises for sale across forums; Unit 42 has not verified the specific intrusion vector or all claims.

incidents.victim: Enterprises via multi-brand vishing extortion (financial services, private equity, law firms)
incidents.vector: The actor tracked as UNC6671 uses IT-helpdesk voice phishing to personal mobile numbers, luring employees to adversary-in-the-middle passkey/MFA portals to steal credentials and session tokens, then runs automated scripts to exfiltrate data from Microsoft 365 and Okta.
incidents.impact: Despite the claimed May 2026 retirement of the BlackFile brand, the group continues under Redact, Pink, Helix and Falcon extortion brands, shifting targeting toward financial and legal firms holding high-value M&A and confidential data; blockchain analysis tied ~$10.7M in BTC to prior BlackFile wallets.

incidents.victim: Fortinet, Sophos and MSSQL edge-device operators
incidents.vector: Large-scale internet-wide password spraying ('FortiBleed') against internet-exposed Fortinet, Sophos and MSSQL services using a curated password list, followed by config extraction, privilege escalation and offline credential cracking to establish persistent admin access.
incidents.impact: An initial-access broker on the Russian-language Exploit[.]in forum claimed responsibility and offered harvested credentials for sale; Unit 42 continues to observe and block attempts and updated its threat brief on Aug 18.

incidents.victim: Ransomware victims contacted by 'Ransom Busters'
incidents.vector: A ransomware affiliate emails victims mid-incident posing as a data-recovery service claiming access to ransomware groups' admin panels, offering to delete stolen data and provide decryption keys for a $20,000-$60,000 fee paid in Bitcoin.
incidents.impact: GuidePoint assessed with moderate confidence that 'Ransom Busters' is a single affiliate working across DragonForce, Settra and Anubis operations, attempting to divert ransom payments outside the normal RaaS structure; victims cannot verify any data is actually deleted.

incidents.victim: Undisclosed organizations (TwinLoot campaign)
incidents.vector: A Python-based modular framework ('TwinLoot') runs its entire command-and-control from inside Microsoft Azure/365 — using SharePoint and the Graph API for C2, Teams TURN relays for interactive access, and the victim's own Edge browser to blend in — while harvesting credentials via fake lock screens and achieving fileless persistence.
incidents.impact: Ontinue discovered the framework during a July campaign; it combines Microsoft 365 dead-drop C2, Teams relay abuse and headless-browser transport in a single implant with a reverse SOCKS5 pivot, defeating controls based on domain reputation or IP blocking.

incidents.victim: Berlin state government (urban development and mobility ministries)
incidents.vector: Attackers allegedly exploited a vulnerability in the IT systems of one of the affected ministries, according to German broadcaster RBB.
incidents.impact: Two Berlin state ministries were disconnected from the city government network as a precaution, cutting email and internet access and disrupting housing-benefit and education-assistance processing at some district offices; scope and data impact remain undisclosed.

incidents.victim: University of Texas at San Antonio
incidents.vector: Threat activity detected at the edge of the university's academic network over the weekend; the vector was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: UTSA (40,000 students) took systems including phones offline, extended payment deadlines, and planned a full password reset days before classes began; the university said no evidence of data access or exfiltration was found and no group claimed the attack.

incidents.victim: 1,100+ companies targeted for fraudulent remote employment
incidents.vector: North Korean IT workers (tracked as PurpleDelta, likely operating from Shenzhen, China) use 22+ fabricated personas, AI-generated photos, custom ChatGPT assistants, forged IDs, anti-detect browsers and real-time AI interview tools to secure remote developer roles.
incidents.impact: One cluster applied to over 1,100 companies (up to 60+ applications/day) and was likely actively employed at ten or more organizations, presenting an ongoing insider threat while funneling earnings to the North Korean regime through facilitators and shell companies.

incidents.victim: French Directorate General of Public Finance (tax agency)
incidents.vector: A hacker using the handle 'ZeroBytes' breached the agency between June and July and exfiltrated taxpayer records before access was cut off.
incidents.impact: Tax information on more than 678,000 French citizens was stolen; the actor claimed to have been downloading data on up to 20 million citizens when the intrusion was detected.

incidents.victim: Wildberries (Russia's largest online retailer)
incidents.vector: Ukraine's GUR claimed a cyberattack against Wildberries' IT systems, timed alongside a physical drone strike on the company's Koledino logistics hub near Moscow.
incidents.impact: GUR said the attack disrupted customer-service channels and partially destabilized payment infrastructure; the incident illustrates how commercial firms are pulled onto the digital battlefield during the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

incidents.victim: Bluesky and GitHub
incidents.vector: Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks flooding the platforms with junk traffic.
incidents.impact: An Iranian hacktivist group calling itself '313 Team' claimed DDoS attacks that caused prolonged outages at Bluesky (Sunday) and GitHub (Monday); the group ran a similar wave in April 2026.

incidents.victim: Colombia Ministry of Justice
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack against Ministry systems, following a national CERT warning that ransomware groups had increased their focus on Colombia.
incidents.impact: The attack disrupted systems supporting illicit-drug monitoring and legal processes, striking days before the country's presidential transition and installation of a new government.

incidents.victim: Consumers of payment and shopping platforms (Shopify, PayPal, Apple, Klarna, banks)
incidents.vector: The 'JWR' phishing framework impersonates 44 checkout/login pages and keeps an encrypted WebSocket open so operators can steer victim sessions live, capturing card data, SSNs, ID/passport images, 2FA codes and device fingerprints; delivered via SMS lures posing as toll and postal authorities.
incidents.impact: Talos assesses JWR (medium confidence) as a variant of the Chinese-speaking 'The Outsider' PhaaS platform, deployed in real-world smishing campaigns across Southeast Asia and the Middle East; its real-time design lets operators bypass MFA on demand.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian IT and system administrators
incidents.vector: A GRU sub-group (tracked as UAC-0145) poses as recruiters on job portals, contacts IT professionals via Telegram, and delivers Windows or Linux malware through fake interview tasks and downloadable apps.
incidents.impact: CERT-UA said the campaign began in May and remains ongoing, likely aimed at harvesting credentials to pivot into managed company and government networks for intelligence collection or supply-chain access — adopting fake-interview tactics long used by North Korea and Iran.

incidents.victim: 165+ organizations using Snowflake (incl. AT&T, Ticketmaster, Neiman Marcus)
incidents.vector: Between February and October 2024, the actor 'Judische' (Connor Moucka) and co-conspirators used stolen credentials to access Snowflake customer accounts that lacked multi-factor authentication, then extorted victims by threatening to publish stolen data.
incidents.impact: Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud, wire fraud, aggravated identity theft and conspiracy, admitting theft of call/text records of 100M+ AT&T customers and billions of records from 165 organizations; conspirators made over $2.5M in ransom payments and re-extorted victims.
